record.binding_note: 1 Mbps sustained is about 0.32 TB per month, so the speed cap fails 1 TiB long before any byte quota could.

identity_cost.detail: Registration and per-day billing in 'kai coins'; the free tier is limited to one purchase per customer.

record.reliability_note: Runs frps 0.35.1, an old release; nothing about uptime is published.
record.confidence_note: Numbers are from the site's extracted plan table; a direct read of the order page would raise the rung.

evidence.proved: free tier is 1 Mbps, 1 port, unlimited traffic claim, one per customer

record.notes: The 'unlimited traffic' label is attached to a 1 Mbps pipe, which is the recurring pattern: unlimited bytes at a rate that cannot deliver them. 1 Mbps is 328 GB per month at full duty.

extras.wg_detail: An frps 0.35.1 endpoint; UDP proxying is an frp feature, but the plan table does not confirm that UDP is enabled for the free port.
